Introduction

According to Dr. Pratipala Bhatia! Mufja’s nephew Maharajadhiraja Kaviraja Sista

Siromani DhareSvara, Sri Bhojadeva was first and foremost a man of great learning, a
versatile scholar, a polymath indeed, for he has been credited with works in almost every
branch of knowledge. According to Ajada? who wrote a commentary named Padakaprakasa
on Sarasvati Kanthabharana’, Bhoja wrote 84 works giving them names with his own titles
and binds. Prabhacandra Suri Prabhavaka Carita refers to Bhoja’s works in several
branches of learning. Of the works ascribed to him, the authorship of the following can be
traced with Rajamartamda a commentary on Patafijali’s YogasUtra, Sarasvati Kanthabharana
(grammar) and Sarasvati Kanthabharana (Poetics),  Srngara Prakasa (Poetics and

Dramaturgy)

Tattva Prakasa (a manual on Agamic Saivas), Brhadrajamartangda

(dharmasastra grantha), Rajamrganka” (medicine), and a work on Astronomy (1042 A.D.)

Dr. Mahesh Singh also details the works of Bhoja as under :-

Samardngana Stradhdra is a voluminous treatise dealing with technical subjects such
as town planning, house architecture, temple architecture and sculptural subjects like
Pratima Laksama, Iconography, Iconometry, Iconoplastic art together with Mudras, the

different hand poses and the poses of the body as well as the postures of legs. It deals with
the canons of painting and devotes a big chapter to the art of mechanical contrivances, the
yantras. The Yukti Kalpataru (also architecture, arts and crafts) Stmgara mafijari katha (an
akhyayika in prose). The Vyavahara-mafijari referred to by Vimalabodha, a commentator of
Mahabharata Camptramayana or Bhoja Camp, Avani Kumara Sataka (having two Prakrta
poems engraved on a stone slab in Bhojasala at Dhara) each having 109 stanzas in
Aryamitra! Vidvajfanavallabha PraSna Jflana (predictions on dreams), Nama Malika and
Salihotra (lexicography and veterinary science). A work on music quoted by N.P.
Cakravarty records two Prakrta poems engraved on a stone slab in the Bhojasala.

### Chapter 1: Mahasamagamana

In both the instances TT has been taken as mountain as well as a tree. समराङ्गणसूत्रधारम्‌ - 7h९€ 1ऽ
apparent paradox in the affinity of the title with the subject matter. The entire work deals with
the Hindu Science of Architecture but the title means - The Architect of the battle field. For this -
The learned article of Dr, U.N. Upadhyaya entitled - “Skandhavara of Ancient Cities’ Journal
of the Ganganatha Jha, Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeeth, Allahabad-2 pp.11-17 VoL XLL. JanuaryDecember 1985 parts 1-4.

The summary of the article runs as under : In Ancient times, the military camps (Skandhavara)
played a prominent role in the establishment and development of cities. Before commencing a
site was selected to serve as a base for military operations against enemies. These bases
gradually grew into well developed cities. Dr. Upadhyaya has based his article mainly on B.B.
Datt’'s Town planning in Ancient India, p.39 saying - Itwas almost an invariable principle
emphasised by the Silpasastras that each new ruling dynasty layout own capital. Here new
capital as suggested by Mr. Dutt must have developed from Skandhavara’s site which possessed
all requisite characteristics of a planned city.

establishment of the camp translated as setting up of the camp by R.P. Kangle pp. 501-503 KAS
Part IL (Kautilltyam Arthasastram Part L p.233 and Part IL English Translation and Notes,
Bombay University 1960 and 1963 Dr. Upadhyaya quotes his own text which has his point
illustrated in Arthasastra Pt-LIX p.154 which actually is Pt-LX.1.p.233 (R.P.Kangle text) and
p.103 part IL 8-15 Adhikaranas, edited by T.Ganapati Sastri.

Dr. Upadhyaya's version:- Arthasdstra also confirms that site selection sarhskara for
Skandhavara was invariably performed by Nayaka and Mauhtrttikalh (astrologers) who
measured a circular or square site for the Skandhavara with a provision of four gateways, Six
roads, ditches, parapitwalls, watch towers which probably formed the essential parts of the

The word Prthvi is called the female child of Prthu, It already indicates the living beings in the
 planetary world possibility of such beings can be on the planets which are originated through the
` two forces i.e. Agni and Soma, active and receptive forces. The word ‘““Prthvi’’ also conveys the

six-fold physical development of the being viz., Asti, Jayate, Vardhate, Viparinamate,
Apaksiyate and Mriyate considered in Vedanta. This is the cycle of death and rebirth.
The word ““Prthvt’’ is derived from the root “‘prath’’ lo expand. The planetary world of the
space is the result of expansion of the force ofgravity from the gacial boiler, where, it was
centralised. Diversification is called churning. Thus Prthvi itself denotes the expanding nature of
the planetary world. .The weakest position of it i.e. force of gravity will bring again vacuum and
he centralisation will take place. So the word Prthvi denotes the planetary world expanded
directly and not the earth, as we believe in the sense of bhiimi. The milching of the earth cow by
“various classes also denotes the proper placement and order at all levels in the planetary world.
Prthu, the mythical king in ‘the Puranic story is associated with kingship. who establishes
, inhabitations develops regional division such as village, city etc., regularises the way of life of
the subjects and makes the Earth smooth by removing hilly areas to make advancement in the
agriculture. He becomes the first king, elected by the tribal kings. He earns the epithet Adiraja,
and Rajaraja, these all Prthu’s adventures are important from the cultural point of view. Here I
discuss Prthu vainya from the astronomical point of view. So [ take the word Prthvi formed from
the root prath to expand. The earth is the result of gacial form turned into solid form, through
liquid one. The gradual changes reflected in the Varaha theory of the Puranas. All five Varahas
are the stages of such gradual development. Prthvi is the result. Space is the place for change.
Apa, Teja and Vayu all three elements have played vital role in transference of the gacial form
` into solid one. Earth is formed by contraction and not expansion, So the word Prthvi for bhumi
neither suits to its connotation of expansion nor to its scientific development. Astronomically the
word “‘PrthvT’’ denotes the expansion of the whole planetary world. Thus, the whole, Prthu
` Vainya episode seems very important from the astronomical point of view, the root “ven” is
meant for constant contraction and expansion or motion at initial stage. The brightness and
shining of this element of it made Sun, Soma, Indra and Venus. Seven seers Dhruva Nisada etc.
= are the astronomical points of the present astronomical world. On the other side, there is black
and shining element. In future, the whole expansion will result in great vacuum by contraction at
the loss of gravity force caused from over expansion.

pompous platitude. The one knowing the procedure, with the rite of offering of materials of
worship, the house owner may propitiate the material arrived and the Lord of the Earth may
adore the material such as the adamant, the weapon and the flag.

On verses 110-114, 115, 116 - Dr. Raghavan says as under :-

The sixth series taken up by Bhoja in the Kridartha class is the fountain i.e. varl-yantra
described in some details by Somadeva and dealt with by Bhoja not only here, but also
earlier under palace architecture. Movment in the Var yantra is fourfold -           |

(a) a downward flow from am overhead tank for which a pata-yantra or water fall
machine, is to be used                Ce

(b) Samanadika is for the release of water at a higher level from tanks placed at that
level.                                                                                                    -

(c) Patasamaucchraya is a contrivance using bored columns for letting down water from
a height and then taking it up through columns placed aslant and

(d) the last, Ucchraya in which water from a well or in a canal on the ground is sent up
by a device (Verses 110-114).                                                                 i

An artificial object which was probably common in Bhoja’s time is a wooden elephant
which Bhoja describes twice; earlier he cited it as an example of various wonderful effects
that could be achieved through yantras (verses 72-73). It occurs here again under yantras
based on the principle of sending water upward. Uccharya (verse 1]5), this wooden
elephant drinks water placed in a vessel, any amount of it and neither the intake nor the
water taken in is perceivable on the same Ucchiya principle of circulation of water on the
same level is based the underground conduit which brings water to a tank from a distant
source; water conduits in general are described earlier also in chapter 18 in connection with
city and residence Bhoja translates Dharagrha as shower bower in a garden.

रथस्य पार्श्वयोर्लेखाः कर्तव्याश्चोभयोरपि॥
On the Bhadra Rathika, one rnay create of varied norm. In the two flanks of the Ratha
this deserves to be created on each sides,

वेदिकास्य विधातव्या भागमेकं समुन्नता।
ग्रीवा तावद्‌ भागमेकमण्डकं द्विपदोदयम्‌॥।
Vedika of this deserves to be created elevated by a part Griva however, deserves to be
created of one part and Andaka of two parted Udaya.

कुर्यात्‌ सामलसारिं च चर्भिकां सार्थभागिकाम्‌।
कलशस्त्रिपदः कार्यो बीजपूरं बहिस्ततः॥
One may create Candriké accompanied by Amalasari of a half part, Kalasa of part triad

deserves to be created and Buyapraka on the exterior.
